title: When a Claim Is Taken under the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans and the Ground Recorded for Refusing It
content:
A claim on a plan of the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans is answered for only where the peril claimed is among the perils the coverage answers for, and a peril the coverage lists as excluded is never answered for however sympathetic the circumstances. A claim is opened only while the covering plan stands at active or inspection overdue, and a claim reported while coverage is suspended is taken but not settled until coverage is put right. A theft claim is settled only once a police report reference has been recorded against the claim, and the customer's account of the theft does not stand in for that report. The customer must give their account of the loss within the proof-of-loss window the coverage sets, counted from the date the customer first reported the loss to the chain. The proof-of-loss window is counted in whole calendar days from the day the loss was first reported, that day counting as day zero, and where the last day falls on a day the store does not open the window runs to the next day the store opens.

Where the peril is not covered the claim is refused under the excluded peril ground; where the coverage had lapsed for want of inspection it is refused under the inspection lapse ground; where the term had run out it is refused under the outside term ground; and exactly one ground is recorded.

## Points of judgement

- **The standing of the plan.** The plan record governs. A plan standing at active or at inspection overdue admits a claim being opened; a plan standing at suspended does not bar the claim being taken, but nothing is settled on it until the coverage is put right.
- **Authority.** The peril answered for is read from the coverage; the police report reference is read from what is recorded against the claim. In neither case does the customer's own account stand in for the record.
- **One ground only.** Where more than one ground would fit the facts, one ground is recorded against the refusal, not several.

## Grounds set out in this note

| Circumstance the coverage meets | Ground recorded |
|---|---|
| the peril claimed is one the coverage does not answer for | the excluded peril ground |
| the coverage had lapsed for want of an inspection | the inspection lapse ground |
| the term of the coverage had run out | the outside term ground |

## Boundary readings of the proof-of-loss window

Take coverage whose proof-of-loss window is 45 calendar days (a hypothetical input) and a loss first reported on a Monday. An account given on the forty-fifth day, counting the day of the report as day zero, comes within the window. An account given on the following day comes outside it, unless the forty-fifth day fell on a day the store does not open, in which case the window runs to the next day the store does open.
